line_items.reasoning: AMD guided Q4 revenue to ~$9.6B (+/- $300M), but reported a record $10.3B — roughly $700M above the top end of the guided range, representing ~34% YoY growth vs. the guided ~25%.

Q4 non-GAAP gross margin was guided to ~54.5%; Data Center operating margins expanded meaningfully and net income hit a record $2.5B, suggesting gross margins came in at or above the 54.5% target (record revenue with strong profitability implies upside to margin guidance).
Data Center was guided up 'double digits' sequentially but came in up 24% QoQ to a record $5.4B, well above a typical double-digit sequential increase.

Embedded was guided to return to growth with double-digit QoQ gains; the full-year report of $17B in embedded design wins (up ~20% YoY) and the record EPS suggest embedded delivered on or exceeded the double-digit recovery target.

Client was guided up sequentially and came in at a record $3.1B, up 34% YoY with desktop CPU sales setting a record for the fourth consecutive quarter — clearly exceeding a modest sequential growth guide.

Gaming was guided down 'strong double digits' sequentially due to holiday semi-custom pull-forward; the reported results are consistent with this expectation, and the risk item confirms the console cycle decline trajectory was anticipated.

Non-GAAP opex was guided to ~$2.8B but came in at ~$3.0B (up 42% YoY), a ~$200M overage vs. guidance, with analysts flagging persistent upward creep — the other items (tax rate, share count, net interest) lack explicit contradicting data so opex is the primary miss here.
